title: helm-tenant-rotation-race-and-snapshot-recovery-hotpatch
creator: Maya Chen
description: Multiple on-prem customers reported post-upgrade failures after applying the operator Helm chart v0.9.2 -> v0.9.3. Symptoms included long reconciliation loops, stuck Helm finalizers on tenant CRs, leader-election turnover across nodes, and in some cases tenant failover to read-only state. This ticket tracks investigation, immediate hotpatch, rollout plan, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps: 1) Install operator v0.9.2 in a VPC/private cluster with multiple node agents and >10 tenant CRs
2) Trigger a secret rotation for tenant credentials during a Helm upgrade (simulate automated external secret rotation)
3) Perform helm upgrade to operator v0.9.3 with hooks enabled (pre/post hooks that touch tenant finalizers)
4) Observe operator reconcile storms, API 409s on CR update, and Helm release stuck status in helm-history
5) Confirm some tenant CRs retain finalizers and nodeagent heartbeats are missing, causing degraded tenant traffic
investigation_summary: Oncall and SRE reproduced the issue in an isolated cluster. Logs show a race between the operator's post-upgrade hook that patches tenant CR finalizers and an async secret-rotation callback from nodeagent that updates the same CR annotation. When the patch collides with an in-flight update, the operator retries and leaves Helm hooks in a partially-applied state. The operator's reconcile logic then re-enqueues the CR repeatedly because it assumes finalizer removal is idempotent but does not account for partial update errors. Several customers hit this path concurrently, amplifying controller queue backlog and causing leader-election churn.
root_cause: A non-transactional sequence during upgrade: Helm hook + operator reconcile + external nodeagent secret rotation update operating on the same tenant CR without optimistic conflict handling. The operator attempted a remove/replace of a finalizer set but did not re-read the latest resource version before retrying, leading to 409 conflicts and stale local state. Helm left hooks marked pending when the controller stalled.
proposed_fix: 1) Immediate hotpatch (v0.9.3-hotfix1): make finalizer operations optimistic by reading latest resourceVersion before patch, use server-side apply for idempotent updates, and add a short lock (in-memory per-tenant) to serialize upgrade-hook vs nodeagent annotation updates.
rollout_plan: Phase A - canary: push v0.9.3-hotfix1 to a small set of low-risk tenants (internal cluster + 1 customer staging) with feature gate 'safe-upgrade-serialization' enabled. Monitor controller queue depth, helm release states, and tenant traffic for 2 hours. Phase B - ramp: if canary healthy, enable across all private clusters during low-traffic windows with automatic rollback to v0.9.2 in case of regressions.
immediate_actions_taken: Applied a manual migration job that removed stale helm finalizers from affected tenant CRs in 3 customer clusters (runbook executed)
Restarted operator controller pods with a temporary backoff patch to reduce reconcile storm frequency
Opened an urgent hotfix branch and submitted PR #11429 for server-side apply and resourceVersion checks
Notified account teams and provided tailored runbooks to affected customers

postmortem_notes: Containment: manual finalizer cleanup and operator restarts stabilized customers within 30-90 minutes
Customer impact: several customers experienced degraded write availability; no customer data loss observed
Root cause classification: race condition between upgrade hook and external secret-rotation flow; operator not using optimistic concurrency safely
Key lesson: upgrades that touch control-plane visible CR fields must be made idempotent and defensively concurrent
